title: Accreditation vs Certification vs Registration
shortDescription: The deepest possible dive into the single distinction this entire subject keeps coming back to — six related concepts, one table, and the traps built around them.
genZNote: If you only remember one table from this whole subject, make it this one.

rows: Accreditation
A body's technical COMPETENCE to perform a specific activity, within a defined scope
NABL accrediting a medical laboratory against ISO 15189
An accreditation body (NABL, NABH)
Certification
Conformity of a management system, product, or person to a specific standard
A hospital's ISO 9001 certificate
A certification body (often itself accredited)
Registration
A basic administrative listing or recording, often without independent technical assessment
A laboratory registered with a local regulatory department
A registering authority
Inspection
A one-time or periodic examination against defined criteria, with a pass/fail or graded outcome
A food-safety inspection of a facility
An inspection body or regulator
Audit
Systematic verification against a standard or the organisation's own documented procedures
An internal audit of a lab's SOP compliance
Internal auditors, or an external audit team
Assessment
The formal evaluation activity accreditation/certification bodies use to make their decision
NABL's on-site technical assessment of a laboratory
Trained assessors appointed by the accreditation/certification body

sections.heading: Why the Layering Matters
sections.body: Notice the layering: a certification BODY can itself be accredited (by a body like NABCB). An accreditation body's own competence is, in turn, benchmarked against ISO/IEC 17017/17011-type requirements for accreditation bodies themselves, and recognised through international cooperation (GACI, APAC). Accreditation sits structurally 'above' certification in this sense — it's often the mechanism that gives certification its credibility in the first place.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Accreditation, certification, registration, inspection, audit, and assessment are six related but distinct conformity-assessment activities, differing in what they demonstrate and who performs them.
keyFacts: Accreditation = competence to perform an activity, within a defined scope.
Certification = conformity of a system/product/person to a standard.
Registration = a basic administrative listing, often without independent technical assessment.
A certification body can itself be accredited — accreditation often underpins certification's credibility.
commonConfusion: People often use 'accredited', 'certified', and 'registered' as interchangeable praise words in everyday speech — in an exam context, each has a precise, distinct technical meaning.

highYieldFacts: Accreditation bodies can accredit certification bodies — the two concepts nest, they don't compete.
Registration is generally the lowest-assurance of the six concepts — often no independent technical assessment at all.
commonTraps: Treating registration as equivalent in rigour to accreditation — registration is typically administrative, not a competence assessment.
Assuming inspection includes ongoing surveillance the way accreditation/certification do — inspection is often a single point-in-time judgement.
mustRemember: Accreditation → competence. Certification → conformity. Registration → administrative listing. Inspection → point-in-time judgement.

confusedTerms.distinction: Accreditation assesses a body's COMPETENCE to perform a technical activity. Certification assesses CONFORMITY of a system, product, or person to a standard. Certification bodies are themselves often accredited.
Registration is typically a basic administrative listing, often without independent technical assessment. Accreditation involves ongoing, assessed technical competence evaluation.

possibleQuestions: Differentiate accreditation, certification, registration, and inspection with one real-world example each.
Why can a certification body itself be accredited? What does that add?

options: NABL assessing a lab's competence against ISO 15189
An external body confirming a hospital's ISO 9001 quality-management system conforms to the standard
A regulator inspecting a pharmacy once a year
A lab being listed in a government registry
questions.explanation: Confirming conformity of a management system to a standard is certification.

questions.prompt: Which of the six concepts (accreditation, certification, registration, inspection, audit, assessment) typically involves the LEAST independent technical assessment?
questions.explanation: Registration is often a basic administrative listing, without the technical competence evaluation accreditation/certification require.

questions.prompt: True or False: A certification body can itself be accredited by an accreditation body.
questions.explanation: Yes — accreditation bodies like NABCB accredit certification bodies, adding a layer of independently verified credibility.
